title: Proof of Euler’s 1747 Conjecture on Sums of Integers with Restricted Prime Factors
whyItMatters: Four Purdue researchers and OpenAI Codex posted a proof of Euler’s 279-year-old 1747 conjecture to Goldbach that every n ≡ 2 (mod 4) sums two numbers whose prime factors are all ≡ 1 (mod 4).
summary: Posted to Hexagon on November 12, 2026 (hexagon:2611.00370v1), Purdue University researchers Will Howe, Grant Huffman, Jensen Kohlmeyer, and Liam Kruer—disclosing that OpenAI Codex generated the mathematical argument, performed the exact calculations, and drafted the manuscript under their direction—claimed a full proof of Leonhard Euler’s May 6, 1747 conjecture to Christian Goldbach: every positive integer n ≡ 2 (mod 4) can be written as a + b where every prime factor of a and b is ≡ 1 (mod 4) (allowing 1). While Dietmann and Elsholtz (2019) proved the result for sufficiently large n without an explicit threshold, Codex’s proof averages Hurwitz-quaternion four-square representations over a nonsplit torus normalizer, invoking the weight-two Ramanujan–Petersson bound via Jacquet–Langlands and Deligne to obtain an explicit threshold n ≥ 64⁴ = 16,777,216, paired with an exact arithmetic sieve covering all 4,194,304 cases below (independently reproduced by whataifound.org).
technicalHighlights: Resolves the explicit threshold gap left by Dietmann–Elsholtz (2019) on a 279-year-old conjecture posed by Euler to Goldbach in 1747.
Combines Hurwitz quaternion norms, nonsplit torus averaging, and explicit Jacquet–Langlands / Deligne Hecke bounds to drop the analytic threshold to 64⁴ = 16,777,216.
Finite arithmetic sieve covering all 4,194,304 integers n ≡ 2 (mod 4) below 64⁴ was independently recomputed and confirmed.
caveats: No Lean formalization yet; while the finite sieve certificate up to 16.77M has been independently reproduced, the explicit constants in the analytic Hecke/Jacquet–Langlands estimate above 64⁴ still await specialist peer review.

scoreRationale.foundational: Completes a classic 279-year-old additive number theory conjecture from Euler’s correspondence with Goldbach by making the asymptotic bound effective.
scoreRationale.ripple: Illustrates effective explicitization of automorphic Hecke bounds combined with exact computational certificates by AI coding agents.
scoreRationale.verification: Finite computational certificate independently verified, but the analytic estimate above 64⁴ is unrefereed and not formalized in Lean.
scoreRationale.velocity: OpenAI Codex generated both the analytic quaternion/Hecke strategy and the exact finite verification sieve.
